title: Kernel hint-tiering and gradual warmup strategy for cold-start and mixed-length flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Cold workers and model variants experience a cold-start penalty when kernel selection probes and microbenchmarks run on first requests. Mixed-length traffic makes it hard to pick a single kernel policy. Goal: design a hint-tiering + gradual warmup controller that minimizes cold-start latency, bounds probing cost, and converges quickly to a per-worker kernel policy that is both architecture- and sequence-length-aware. Key idea: classify kernel hints into confidence tiers (exploratory / safe / preferred), run constrained microbench probes during a limited warmup budget per worker, and progressively shift workers from conservative to preferred hints as empirical latency and cost signals converge.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start median latency improvement >= 20% on a mixed-seqlen benchmark compared to current baseline for first 100 requests
Probe CPU/GPU overhead < 3% of serving compute during warmup windows on average
No regression in p99 latency for steady-state traffic after rollout (<= 2% change)
Telemetry shows warmup convergence (stable kernel choice) within N=50 requests for >80% of workers on standard workload
Automated safety rollback (canary) triggers on increase in error-rate or p99 latency beyond thresholds
technical_notes: Hint tiers: exploratory (cheap probes, low-risk kernels), safe (fallback-compatible kernels), preferred (cost/latency-optimal discovered kernels).
Warmup budget: per-worker probe budget expressed as 'probe_token_budget' and 'probe_request_quota' to cap cost and SLO risk (default: 10k tokens, 20 requests).
Probe schedule: staggered microbench on prefills during low-util phases; if traffic is bursty, switch to passive observation mode and defer probes to idle cycles.

Sequence-length bucketing: maintain lightweight reservoir sketches per worker for prefill and decode seqlen histograms; use bucketed cost model to evaluate candidate kernels instead of raw avg latency.
Confidence scoring: blend empirical latency quantiles with model compatibility score and historical stability to produce a kernel hint score; map score -> hint tier.
Gradual promotion: workers move tiers only after 'stability windows' (e.g., 10 successful requests within target p95 margin) to avoid oscillation under mixed traffic.
Failure safety: all promoted kernels must support fast fallback to safe tier; implement atomic kernel swap with KV cache compatibility checks.
Cost control: probe trials are charged to a 'warmup pool' and rate-limited per region/customer to avoid billing surprises.
Edges: for tiny-prefill-only workloads (<= 8 tokens) default to minimal-kernel chain to avoid probe noise; for long streaming decode bursts prioritize kernel throughput profiles.
Compatibility: integrate with existing runtime kernel-advisor interface via a new 'warmup_hint' signal on worker bootstrap and on route handoff.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit microbench harness to validate probe timings on representative GPUs and two model families (decoder-only / encoder-decoder).
Phase 1 (canary small): enable on 1% of hosted workers, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, probe overhead, and warmup convergence signals for 72 hours.
Phase 2 (canary expand): 10% workers with gradual increase, enable additional telemetry flags for token-phase histograms and per-worker chosen kernel history.
Phase 3 (region roll): roll to non-critical regions and Dedicated pools with opt-in flag for customers; collect cost delta and customer feedback.
Phase 4 (global): full rollout with automated heuristics enabled by default but with a tenancy-level opt-out and adjustable probe budgets.
Rollback criteria: >5% relative increase in p99 latency, >1% increase in 5xx error rate, or unexplained increases in token cost; automatic rollback to 'safe' tier for affected workers.
